pr.title: Merge stores entry by entry, and keep each entry's earlier secrets
pr.head: 457108aeaa304224e10539728e7a6cbc625a14bb

summary: multipass keeps every password in one text document, encrypted as one age file. Each save replaces the whole file, so when two Macs each change a copy, nothing can combine them and one copy's changes are lost. The next plan in line, vault-key, writes every save as a new file and needs a way to combine the files it finds into one store. This pull request supplies that combination.
It does so with a new store text, format 3, and a merge function:

1. Every entry records when it last changed. A modified line holds the time in milliseconds. A change is stamped one millisecond past the newest stamp in the store it was made from, so a change made after seeing another always wins, even when clocks disagree.
  2. Removing an entry leaves a tombstone. rm keeps the name with modified and deleted, so a merge can tell a removal from an entry it has never seen. For 30 days the tombstone also keeps the whole removed entry, and multipass restore <name> brings it back.
  3. Stores merge entry by entry. Store::merge keeps each name's newest version, so every Mac that merges the same files writes the same store. Nothing outside the tests calls it yet; vault-key is its first caller.
  4. Each entry keeps its earlier secrets. previous-secret and previous-otp lines hold replaced secrets and setup keys. A merge turns the losing version's secret into history, so a merge never drops a secret. multipass history lists the dates, and multipass get --previous <n> prints one.

multipass still reads formats 1 and 2, whose entries read as modified 0, and writes format 3. An older multipass refuses a format 3 store with the store uses format 3, but this multipass reads formats 1 and 2.
This head also merges main, which added the installer and multipass upgrade. The merge keeps both sides of the one conflict in src/main.rs, and upgrade refuses --previous like the other entry flags.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Stamp: an entry's modified value, milliseconds since 1970.
  • Version: one name's state in one store, a live entry or a tombstone, with its stamp and history.
  • Tombstone: a removed entry, kept as its name, modified, deleted, and history lines, with the removed entry's fields after deleted for 30 days.
  • History: an entry's earlier secrets and setup keys, each with the time it was replaced.
  • Cutoffs: the three times before which Store::expire drops things, as the CLI opens the store and as to_text writes it.

cards.title: What is kept, and for how long
cards.html:
WhatKept
A live entry's earlier secrets and setup keysThe newest 10 of each, or every one replaced in the past year, whichever is more
A removed entry, whole, for restore30 days
A removed entry's secrets and setup key, as history30 days
A removed entry's marker120 days

multipass applies each limit as it opens the store, so no command shows a value past its limit. The file itself drops the value at the next save, so age -d can still show it until then.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The review of f7a68da asked for two changes to how rm was described: a removed secret could outlive the 30 days the README promised, and undoing a removal brought back only the secret.
  • This head fixed both in code. Store::expire runs as the CLI opens the store, and restore brings back the whole entry. Both threads are resolved, and the review of 0aa2ae4 is clean.
  • fmt, clippy, tests, the dependency check, and CI passed. Stock age was not installed where the review ran, so no store from this head was decrypted with age -d in the review.
  • 7505c25 merges main, which brought in the installer and multipass upgrade. The merge resolved one conflict in src/main.rs, keeping both sides' lines, and made upgrade refuse --previous. Its review is clean, with two README suggestions: update the line count, and warn that upgrade 0.1.0 installs a release that cannot open a format 3 store.
  • 457108a updates the README's line count to about 2,600, which matches the code. Its incremental review is clean. The downgrade warning is still a suggestion, and it does not block.

groups.title: Format 3, history, and the merge
groups.kicker: The store module: the new text, the version type, and how two stores combine.
intro: All of the change's logic lives in src/store.rs. The store maps each name to a Version: a live entry or a tombstone, its stamp, and its History. A tombstone's removed field keeps the removed entry for 30 days. Every change goes through insert, remove, or restore, which take a stamp and move the replaced secret and setup key into the history. The old get_mut, which changed an entry without a stamp, is gone.

Version::join is the merge of two versions of one name. It keeps the one with the newer stamp, breaks a tie by comparing the versions' text without their history, and takes the union of both histories plus each version's own secret and setup key. A losing value is dated by its own version's stamp, not the winner's, which is what keeps the merge commutative, associative, and idempotent: two Macs that merge the same files in any order write the same store.

Nothing is pruned in the merge. Store::expire applies the three cutoffs. The CLI runs it as it opens the store, and to_text runs it on a copy before writing, so the merge stays a pure union and no command shows a value the next write would drop.

checks.text: The plan's § 2.1 table is the format's definition. A field line always starts with a tab, and names escape tab, newline, carriage return, and backslash, so an entry name can never read as a modified, deleted, or previous-* line.

files.note: The format 3 text, Version and History, stamps, Store::merge, expire and restore, and the reader for formats 1 to 3.

checks.text: The merge laws hold with history and removed entries included. The review walked join and normalize by hand, and merge_is_commutative_associative_and_idempotent passed over 3,000 generated triples that include tombstones with and without a removed entry.

restore brings back the whole removed entry within 30 days of the removal, measured by its stamp. The review restored an entry's username, notes, and setup key with a release build, and restore_brings_back_the_whole_entry_for_30_days checks the boundary.

A name added again after the 30 days takes no removed secret back, even when no write ran in between. re_adding_after_30_days_leaves_the_removed_secrets_behind covers the case the first review reproduced.
expire holds every cutoff rule, and expiring_leaves_what_a_write_and_a_read_leave checks that it leaves exactly the store to_text writes. A caller that merges must expire each store before the merge.

Malformed lines fail with only their line number. rejects_malformed_text covers a missing or misplaced modified, a field before deleted, a removed entry with neither secret nor otp, and history dated after the entry or with no value.

groups.title: The CLI: stamps, history, and --previous
groups.kicker: How each command stamps its change, the two new ways to read history, and restore.
intro: run reads the clock once, and open expires the store as of that time. Each saving command (add, rm, restore, otp --set, otp --clear) takes a stamp from the store it opened, warns when that stamp is more than a day ahead of the clock, and saves with Cutoffs::at(now).

Two read commands are new. multipass history <name> lists when the entry changed and when each earlier value was replaced, and never shows a value. multipass get <name> --previous <n> prints or copies the nth most recently replaced secret, or with --field otp the setup key. Both also find a removed entry. Without --previous, get still prints the current value.

multipass restore <name> makes a removed entry live again within its 30 days. It refuses a live name with <name> is not removed, an unknown one with no removed entry named <name>, and an expired removal.

files.note: Stamps for each saving command, expiry on open, the history and restore commands, get --previous, and a UTC date formatter.

checks.text: restore refuses a live and an unknown name with errors that show no value. The review saw both against a release build driven with expect.

Errors from previous_value name only a count, such as x has only 2 earlier secrets. The review saw this against a release build driven with expect, and previous_counts_from_the_most_recently_replaced covers it.
history prints dates and no value. history_lists_dates_and_no_values checks that no secret or key appears, and the release build printed only dates.
Every command expires the store here, so a removed secret past its 30 days is gone from every read before any write.

groups.title: README, AGENTS.md, and the plans
groups.kicker: What users and agents are told about format 3 and history.
intro: The README gains a section on getting an earlier password back and on restore, and its recovery example shows format 3, including a tombstone with its removed entry. AGENTS.md says multipass writes format 3 and that the merge must keep its laws with history included. The store-merge plan records the history design, the 30-day decision, expire, and restore, and is marked completed with an outcome. The passkeys plan no longer calls history undecided.

files.note: A new section on earlier passwords and restore, and the recovery example in format 3.

checks.text: This paragraph says when a removed entry stops being found, and that the file drops it only at the next save, which is what the code does.
